State Civil Commitment & Crisis Legal Navigator

              

                While voluntary engagement yields stronger long-term continuity, 37+ states provide emergency civil commitment statutes when a person poses an imminent danger to themselves or others due to severe substance use (Casey's Law & State Statutes Guide):
              

              

                

                  
Washington State — Ricky's Law (ITA Behavioral Health)

                  

                    Allows Designated Crisis Responders (DCRs) to detain individuals gravely disabled or at imminent risk of harm from severe SUD to secure withdrawal management/stabilization (e.g., Lifeline Connections ITA Inpatient & Anne Deacon Center for Hope).
                  

                

                

                  
Florida (Marchman Act) & KY/OH (Casey's Law)

                  

                    Permits spouse, relative, or three adults to petition the court for emergency assessment (typically heard within 14 days under Casey's Law; note that Casey's Law requires petitioners to cover treatment costs if uninsured).
                  

                

              

            


            

              
Family HIPAA & 42 CFR Part 2 Communication Rights

              

                Families are often told "we can't talk to you because of HIPAA." Per HHS Office for Civil Rights Mental Health & Opioid Guidance:
              

              
    
                
  • You can always share information: Neither HIPAA nor 42 CFR Part 2 prevents a clinician from listening to family members or receiving collateral medical/substance history from you.
    • 
                
  • Overdose & Incapacity Exception: Clinicians may notify family members during an acute opioid overdose or medical emergency when the patient is incapacitated.
    • 
                
  • Under-26 Parental Plan Verification: Parents can pre-verify in-network parity benefits under the Mental Health Parity and Addiction Equity Act (MHPAEA) before their adult child signs a Part 2 intake consent.
    •

Production Two-Zone PostgreSQL DDL Schema (`public_directory` + `part2_vault`)

              
Physical & cryptographic isolation between public verified provider records and envelope-encrypted 42 CFR Part 2 patient consents

            

            
          

          
-- ZONE 1: PUBLIC PROVIDER DIRECTORY & VERIFICATION SCHEMA (NO PHI / NO PII)
CREATE SCHEMA public_directory;

CREATE TABLE public_directory.providers (
    provider_id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    npi_number VARCHAR(10) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
    legal_entity_name TEXT NOT NULL,
    provider_type VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL CHECK (provider_type IN ('FACILITY', 'COUNSELOR', 'OTP', 'CCBHC')),
    samhsa_bhsis_id VARCHAR(64) UNIQUE, -- Verified via SAMHSA FindTreatment.gov / N-SUMHSS
    is_part2_program BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,
    asam_levels_offered TEXT[] NOT NULL, -- e.g., {'1.0','2.1','2.5','3.5','3.7'}
    mat_medications TEXT[] NOT NULL,     -- e.g., {'BUPRENORPHINE','METHADONE','NALTREXONE'}
    accepted_payers TEXT[] NOT NULL,     -- e.g., {'WA_APPLE_HEALTH','PREMERA','SLIDING_SCALE'}
    anti_brokering_attestation_signed_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    verification_status VARCHAR(24) NOT NULL CHECK (verification_status IN ('PENDING', 'VERIFIED', 'SUSPENDED'))
);

-- ZONE 2: ISOLATED HIPAA / 42 CFR PART 2 VAULT SCHEMA (ENVELOPE ENCRYPTED)
CREATE SCHEMA part2_vault;

CREATE TABLE part2_vault.part2_consents (
    consent_id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    patient_id UUID NOT NULL,
    consent_category VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL CHECK (consent_category IN (
        'NAMED_PROVIDER_ONLY', 'SINGLE_TPO_CONSENT', 'SUD_COUNSELING_NOTES_ONLY'
    )),
    recipient_provider_ids UUID[] NOT NULL,
    permitted_data_scopes TEXT[] NOT NULL,
    self_pay_plan_restriction BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    redisclosure_notice_attached BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE CHECK (redisclosure_notice_attached = TRUE),
    prohibit_legal_proceedings BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE CHECK (prohibit_legal_proceedings = TRUE),
    patient_signature_hash CHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    signed_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    revoked_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
    status VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('ACTIVE', 'EXPIRED', 'REVOKED'))
);

          24/7 Emergency & Withdrawal Triage
          
Immediate Crisis, Overdose & Medical Detox Guidance

        

        
      


      

        

          
1. Medical Emergency or Suspected Overdose (Call 911)

          

            If someone is unresponsive, breathing slowly, or having a seizure, call 911 immediately and administer Naloxone (Narcan) if opioids may be involved. Washington's Good Samaritan Law protects both caller and patient from drug possession prosecution.
          

        


        

          
2. Alcohol or Benzodiazepine Withdrawal Risk

          

            Do not stop heavy daily alcohol or benzodiazepine (Xanax, Valium, Klonopin, Ativan) use cold turkey without medical supervision—withdrawal can trigger fatal seizures or delirium tremens (NIAAA Navigator). Use a 24/7 Level 3.7/4.0 medical detox center below.
          

        


        

          
Direct 24/7 Helplines & Whatcom / Puget Sound Crisis Stabilization:

          
• 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline: Call or text 988 (988lifeline.org)

          
• SAMHSA National Helpline: 1-800-662-4357 (Free 24/7 Referral)

          
• WA Recovery Help Line: 1-866-789-1511 (Crisis Connections WA)

          
• Bellingham 24/7 Detox & Crisis: Anne Deacon Center for Hope (Whatcom Community Detox) — 2026 Division St, Bellingham, WA (`(360) 676-2020`)
